title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is building the moduli of elliptic curves over Z[1/2] (char ≠ 2) by 'pinnings' (épinglages), i.e. extra structures that kill automorphisms.

- **Legendre pinning (k).** It identifies the quotient conic Σ_E = E/{±1}, with its branch divisor D (the images of 0 and of the 2-torsion), with P^1 and the divisor 0+1+∞+λ. This is the Legendre form y² = x(x−1)(x−λ). Automorphisms ±1 survive.
- **Legendre–Jacobi pinning of level ('échelon') 2 (k,u).** The previous page adds a 'Jacobi' pinning u: a trivialisation of the 3-point set J (nonzero 2-torsion) compatible with Σ_J ≅ P^1_S, sending 0+1+∞ to D_J. The resulting fibred category of pinned curves is rigid. It is equivalent to pairs (t, α), with t a section of U_{0,1} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} and α a unit subject to a condition.

This page.
- **(37)** That stack of groupoids is representable by the scheme U_{0,3} × μ_4^*. Here U_{0,3} is P^1 minus three points, i.e. the λ-line, and μ_4^* = Spec Z[1/2][i] is the scheme of primitive 4th roots of unity. So the fine moduli scheme is the Legendre λ-line base-changed to Z[i,1/2]. This is a connected degree-2 étale cover of the λ-line, reminiscent of the Weil-pairing map Y(4) → μ_4^*.
- **(38)** Over this base the universal pinned curve E has an associated bundle Δ_E. Δ_E is canonically isomorphic to Π_0 := O_{U×μ_4^*}(1)^♮, a twisted form (♮) of O(1) on the conic Σ.
- **(39)** Over μ_4^* the conic bundle Q_{0S} is trivial, since √−1 exists and the relevant norm-type conic acquires a point. Hence the twist disappears, Π_0 ≃ O_{U_{0,3}}(1), canonically pulled back from U_{0,3}.
- **Programme note.** One must make explicit the natural structure (the transcription's 'O-structure'; possibly 'Q-' or 'Θ-structure') attached to pinned/Legendre structures. One must also study the group actions (S_3 on the λ-line, Galois/μ_4 on μ_4^*, and the change-of-pinning group) on U_{0,3} × μ_4^* and on Π_0.
- **Next page.** It confirms the outcome: Legendre 'épi-rigidifications' Δ_{E/S} ≅ O_Σ(1)^♮ form a μ_4-torsor L_{E/S}. Equivalently they are square roots K' of a section of ω, with K'^{⊗2} coming from ω.

Purpose. The aim is a concrete, explicit presentation of the moduli stack M_{1,1}[1/2] as a quotient of the Legendre/level-2 data by finite groups (S_3 × μ_4-type). This fits his 1980s interest in M_{0,4} ↔ M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower.
errors: No outright error is visible. The page is a terse working sketch, and several objects are not defined on the page: Δ_E, the twist ♮, the conic bundle Q_{0S}, and the precise condition on α that cuts O_S^* down to μ_4^*. The claim in (39) depends on the specific conic being split by √−1. That is plausible (e.g. x²+y²=0-type, or a conic determined by a 2-cocycle with values ±1), but it is not checked on the page.
Notation is inconsistent: U_{0,1} on the previous page versus U_{0,3} here, both apparently meaning P^1 minus {0,1,∞}.
The step from (38) to (39) silently drops the μ_4^* factor in the subscript. This is fine only after choosing the trivialisation of Q_{0S}, which is canonical only up to the stated action.

ideas.what: The fibred category of elliptic curves with Legendre–Jacobi level-2 pinning is rigid and represented by (λ-line) × μ_4^* over Z[1/2]
ideas.modern_name: Fine moduli scheme for level-2 structure plus a rigidifying datum; Legendre family over Y(2); Weil-pairing component μ_4^*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre/Jacobi classically; Igusa (1959) for the Legendre family and level structures in char p; Deligne–Rapoport (1973) and Katz–Mazur (1985) for moduli with level structure

ideas.what: Canonical identification of the bundle Δ_E with a twisted O(1)^♮ on the quotient conic, untwisted over μ_4^* because a conic bundle splits once √−1 is present
ideas.modern_name: Brauer class / Severi–Brauer conic bundle Σ = E/±1 and its splitting; theta characteristic-like square roots of ω
ideas.where_published: General conic-bundle/Brauer theory is in 'Le groupe de Brauer' I–III (1968), but not this specific application

ideas.what: Programme to describe actions of the change-of-pinning groups on the moduli scheme and the bundle, i.e. a presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2] as a quotient stack
ideas.modern_name: M_{1,1}[1/2] ≅ [Y(2)/(S_3 × μ_2)]-type presentations; Legendre-form stack presentations
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; e.g. explicit presentations in work on the stack of elliptic curves (Deligne, Mumford 'Picard groups of moduli problems', later Fulton–Olsson)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine computational step in an explicit construction of elliptic-curve moduli via Legendre/Jacobi normal forms and level-2 structure. The content (Legendre family, μ_4^* from √−1 / Weil pairing, splitting of a conic) is classical. The only idiosyncrasy is the 'épinglage' language and the ♮-twisted O(1). Nothing here appears to be a result or connection absent from the literature.
